guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: The Company is raising its full year 2026 outlook for Organic Sales2 growth to 10.0% to 10.5%, compared to its previous outlook of 9.0% to 10.0%, and reaffirming its Adjusted EBITDA2 outlook of $3.3 billion to $3.4 billion. Consistent with prior guidance, the Adjusted EBITDA outlook does not reflect IEEPA tariff refunds, including the $324 million of net tariff benefit through the first nine months of 2026.

desk.headline: Sales up 10.4% to $7.9bn, adjusted EPS $0.44 beat; 2026 organic growth outlook raised, EBITDA outlook kept, $1bn buyback
results: Medline, the largest US maker and distributor of medical-surgical supplies, grew sales 10.4% to $7.9bn (10.5% organic), mainly from existing customers and 2025 contract wins.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.8% to $960m, including an $81m net benefit from refunds of tariffs the Supreme Court struck down; net income slipped 1.2% to $318m on cost inflation and higher expenses.
Own-brand products grew 6.6% with margin up to 25.9%; the distribution arm grew 13.9% but its margin fell to 4.4% from 5.5%.
Nine-month free cash flow was $1.8bn; net leverage fell to 2.5x, a $750m term loan was prepaid in October and a $1bn buyback was approved.

guidance.summary: Medline raised its 2026 organic sales growth outlook and kept its adjusted EBITDA range, which still leaves out the $324m of net tariff refunds booked so far this year.

items.metric: Net sales growth (early view, from call)
Adjusted EBITDA growth (early view, from call)

points: Medline is on track for its $1bn new-customer signings goal for 2026.
Distribution margins should stay around the mid-4% range for the rest of 2026, squeezed by lower rebates on new contracts and higher costs.
Middle East-related cost inflation is now put at about $80m for 2026, with more of it reaching Q4 as dearer stock is sold.
Early 2027 view: high single-digit sales growth but slower EBITDA growth, a larger price rise in Q1 and $80–90m of yearly restructuring savings.
The Tracy distribution centre lost in a fire is due to be replaced by year-end; spending on the business and bolt-on deals come before buybacks.

watch: Whether distribution-arm margins steady as new contracts mature.
How far the Q1 2027 price increase offsets cost inflation.
Use of the new $1bn buyback and further debt repayment.
